reading.body:
Black Forest Labs raised $307.6 million of a $343.3 million offering, its first sale in November 2025 and its filing in June 2026.

The company is a 2024-founded research lab in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany, selling FLUX image models through an API. The raise is large for a lab that is two years old and sells model access rather than compute or data center capacity. The gap between the $343.3 million offered and the $307.6 million sold is about $35.7 million, so the round was not fully subscribed at the time of filing.

What the data does not show is where the money goes. There is no disclosure of headcount, training compute, chip purchases, or data center commitments. For a visual model lab, the binding costs are typically GPU hours and the power and buildings behind them, but nothing here confirms that this raise funds any of it. The filing also gives no valuation, no investor names, and no revenue.

The record covers one Form D filing and a company profile. It does not establish whether Black Forest Labs owns or rents compute, or whether its scaling is constrained by power. On the evidence given, the useful fact is the size and timing of the raise, not what it buys.

profile_text.body:
Black Forest Labs is a research lab founded in 2024 and based in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany. On its own site it describes itself as a frontier AI lab building visual intelligence, meaning models that understand, reason, and act in the world.

The company points users to its FLUX models, which it offers through an API. Its site also lists the terms that govern that work: Developer Terms of Service, FLUX API Service Terms, Self-Hosted Terms of Service, Non-Commercial License Terms, and a Responsible AI Development Policy.
